findings.title: Confirm copy understates the blast radius — the whole destination group is re-graded and re-tagged, not just the moved checks
findings.where: design.md §4 Interaction flow step 3 (confirm copy, both count==null and numeric variants)
findings.problem: The confirm dialog tells the admin 'This re-grades the moved checks against <dest>', but Step 4 (and its side-effect note) re-grade the ENTIRE destination group and overwrite xml_master on every destination row with destXml, including the destination's pre-existing checks. The design admits a destination row holding a different xml_master is silently overwritten and re-graded. For a destructive, bulk, admin-gated operation the confirm dialog must describe the real scope the operator is consenting to.
findings.fix: Change the confirm copy to state the real scope, e.g. 'Move N check(s) for "<source>" into "<dest>". "<source>" will be removed, and all checks under "<dest>" will be re-graded against the "<dest>" master. This can't be undone from here.' (and the analogous count==null variant). This also makes the success copy's distinct moved vs regraded numbers intelligible.

findings.title: canMergeInto typed for string source/dest but UI passes nullable mergeDest
findings.where: design.md §3 canMergeInto(destFileName: string) vs §4 step 3 using RowState.mergeDest (string | null)
findings.problem: canMergeInto takes destFileName: string, but the UI holds mergeDest: string | null. Passing null fails typecheck or, if coerced, isValidMasterName throws on .trim(). The Move-button behavior while mergeDest is null is unspecified.
findings.fix: Specify the guard explicitly: disabled={row.busy || !row.mergeDest || !canMergeInto(m.fileName, row.mergeDest)}, so canMergeInto is only ever called with a non-null string. No signature change needed.

findings.title: Success copy says 'Source removed.' unconditionally even when some destination rows silently failed to re-grade
findings.problem: Step 3 empties the source, Step 4 collects per-row re-grade failures without throwing. If some rows fail, res.regraded is less than the destination group size, yet the copy still says 'Source removed.' with no hint that a subset failed and awaits backfill/retry.
findings.fix: Add a failed/attempted count to MergeMastersResult and, when res.regraded falls short, append a note such as 'Some checks could not be re-graded and will reconcile on the next backfill.'
